bracket: [Textbook error in the QUESTION'S OWN PREMISE, for part (c). The instruction is "justify that the following reactions ARE redox reactions", but in \(4\text{BCl}_3 + 3\text{LiAlH}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 + 3\text{LiCl} + 3\text{AlCl}_3\) NO element changes its oxidation number: boron is \(+3\) on both sides, hydrogen \(-1\) on both sides, and lithium, chlorine and aluminium are unchanged. It is a metathesis (a ligand exchange of hydride for chloride), not a redox reaction. THE READING TURNS ENTIRELY ON HYDROGEN, so both are set out below and the reader should know which they are being asked for. Hydrogen (electronegativity 2.20) is MORE electronegative than both boron (2.04) and aluminium (1.61), so in \(\text{LiAlH}_4\) and in \(\text{B}_2\text{H}_6\) it is \(-1\) and boron stays \(+3\) — that is the analysis below, and it follows the principle the chapter's rules are derived from. Applied LITERALLY, however, the chapter's rule 4 says hydrogen is \(+1\) except in metal hydrides; boron is a metalloid rather than a metal, so a strict reading gives \(\text{H} = +1\) and \(\text{B} = -3\) in \(\text{B}_2\text{H}_6\), which WOULD make the reaction redox, and that is what most answer guides print. **This exercise carries no entry in the printed answer key, so nothing external settles it.** Parts (a), (b), (d) and (e) are genuine redox reactions and are unaffected.]

[Textbook misprint in part (b): the equation does not balance in sulphur. Two \(\text{CuSO}_4\) on the left carry two sulphur atoms, while the single \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) printed on the right carries one. The coefficient should be \(2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), which balances hydrogen at the same time — left \(3 + 4 = 7\), right \(3 + 4 = 7\) — so one correction closes both. The reaction the question asks about is otherwise as printed, and the answer below uses the balanced form.]

[Textbook misprint in part (a): the phosphorus product is printed \(\text{HPO}_2^{-}\), which puts phosphorus at \(+2\). The chapter's own equation 7.46 gives this species as the hypophosphite ion \(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^{-}\), with phosphorus at \(+1\) — so the book contradicts itself between its text and this exercise. The equation below is balanced AS PRINTED, since that is the question set, and the book's own \(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^{-}\) form is given alongside so a reader meeting either version can follow.]

The standard electrode potentials it needs are in **Table 7.1**. The "8.1" is a leftover from an earlier edition in which this chapter was Unit 8 — the same stale numbering that survives elsewhere in the chapter. The table is attached to this question so it can be answered without hunting for it.]
